name: mindtrail-retrieval
description: Synthetic developer-memory corpus: three projects (web shop, ML pipeline, Rust CLI) plus personal preferences. Hand-written by the Mindtrail authors; small and not a substitute for real-world evaluation.

memories.content: The backend API is built with FastAPI and runs on Python 3.12
The primary database is PostgreSQL 16, accessed through SQLAlchemy 2.0
Database schema migrations are managed with Alembic; run `alembic upgrade head` after pulling
The frontend is a React 18 single-page app built with Vite and TypeScript
Payments are processed through Stripe; webhooks land on /api/webhooks/stripe
Integration tests need a running Postgres; start it with `docker compose up db`
Unit tests run with `pytest -x -q` from the repository root
Deployments go through GitHub Actions to Fly.io when a tag matching v* is pushed
Commit messages follow Conventional Commits, and PRs are squash-merged
Never call the Stripe API from the frontend; all payment calls go through the backend
Product images are stored in an S3 bucket and served via CloudFront
Background jobs such as order emails run on Celery with Redis as the broker
API errors are returned as RFC 7807 problem+json responses
Feature flags are managed in LaunchDarkly; the flag for the new checkout is `checkout-v2`
The staging environment is at staging.shop.example.com and resets every night
The release freeze starts on November 20
The release freeze was moved to November 27
The team uses Black for code formatting
Code is formatted with Ruff; Black was removed
The checkout conversion dashboard lives in Metabase
The checkout conversion dashboard moved to Grafana
Production deploys are paused until the Postgres upgrade finishes
Production deploys resumed after the Postgres upgrade
Training data lives in s3://ml-data/raw and is versioned with DVC
Models are trained with PyTorch Lightning on a single A100 GPU
Experiment tracking uses Weights & Biases under the team project `churn-model`
Hyperparameters are defined in Hydra configs under conf/
The evaluation metric we report is AUROC on the held-out 2025 cohort
Feature engineering code is in src/features and must stay free of pandas; use polars
Run the full training pipeline with `make train`
Model artifacts are registered in MLflow before deployment
The serving endpoint is a BentoML service on Kubernetes
Random seeds are fixed to 42 for reproducibility
The baseline model is logistic regression
The baseline model is now a gradient-boosted tree (LightGBM)
Data labeling is done in Label Studio by the annotations team
Notebooks go in notebooks/ and must not be imported by production code
Unit tests run with `pytest tests/ -n auto`
Model deployments happen through Argo CD
The CLI is written in Rust and uses clap for argument parsing
Release binaries are built with cargo-dist for Linux, macOS and Windows
Errors are handled with anyhow in the binary and thiserror in the library crate
Minimum supported Rust version is 1.75
Integration tests use assert_cmd and live in tests/cli.rs
Config files are read from ~/.config/tool/config.toml
Run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` before pushing; CI fails on any warning
The async runtime is tokio, used only in the network module
User prefers concise answers with code first and explanation after
User works on Windows 11 with PowerShell as the default shell
User prefers type hints on all Python functions
User dislikes adding new dependencies without discussing them first
User's editor is VS Code with Vim keybindings
User wants a failing test written before a reported bug is fixed
User's timezone is PST
User moved to Berlin; timezone is now CET
User prefers British English spelling in documentation
User likes small, focused pull requests under 300 lines
